title: EF Core query performance (compiled queries, indexes, execution plans)
hook: Entity Framework Core translates LINQ to SQL. Slow APIs often trace to missing indexes, N+1 queries, tracking overhead, or plans that scan millions of rows after a large customer import.

blocks.text: EF Core builds SQL from LINQ expressions, executes via ADO.NET, and materializes entities or projections. Performance levers include AsNoTracking for read-only APIs, explicit Include vs projection to avoid N+1, compiled queries for hot paths, database indexes matching WHERE and ORDER BY, split queries for large graphs, and reading SQL logs or execution plans. After bulk onboarding inserts millions of rows, statistics drift — queries that used index seeks may regress to scans until UPDATE STATISTICS runs.

entries.plainDefinition: LINQ expression compiled once and reused — reduces query compilation overhead on hot paths.
One query for parent list plus N queries for each child navigation — classic API latency bug.

blocks.text: API slow after large customer onboarding often means new tenant data shifted cardinality — missing composite index on (TenantId, CreatedAt) causes table scans on order lists. EF makes it easy to accidentally Include entire object graphs or return tracked entities from singleton services. Senior interviews expect EXPLAIN/plan literacy, projection to DTO, pagination, and knowing when raw SQL or Dapper beats EF for reporting.

blocks.title: Measure SQL not guesses
blocks.body: Enable EF sensitive logging in dev, use MiniProfiler or OpenTelemetry SQL tags, and verify indexes with actual execution plans before adding Redis cache to mask slow queries.

diagram.title: EF query pipeline to SQL
diagram.source:
flowchart LR
  LINQ[LINQ in service] --> TRAN[Expression translator]
  TRAN --> SQL[SQL command]
  SQL --> DB[(SQL Server)]
  DB --> MAT[Materialize DTO or entity]
  MAT --> API[JSON response]
  IDX[Missing index] -.->|scan| DB

snippet.label: Read-only list with projection and pagination
snippet.explanation: AsNoTracking for reads. Select projects narrow columns — no N+1. Ensure index on (TenantId, CreatedAt DESC). CountAsync is separate query — cursor pagination avoids total on huge tables.

snippet.label: Compiled async query for hot single-row lookup
snippet.explanation: CompileAsyncQuery caches expression translation for repeated calls — valuable on high-RPS GET by id. Still needs primary key index.

snippet.label: Fix N+1 with split query Include
snippet.explanation: AsSplitQuery sends separate SQL for includes — better than single JOIN cartesian product for multiple collections. Best: Select DTO with nested list in one projection when possible.

snippet.label: Diagnostics — index and plan after bulk onboarding
snippet.explanation: Onboarding bulk load skews statistics — optimizer chooses scan. Index plus updated stats often fix API slow without code change.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Returning IQueryable from repository without pagination cap. Filtering in memory after ToListAsync. Singleton DbContext (not thread-safe). Caching tracked entities. Select * via entity when DTO needs three fields.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: Application Insights dependency duration on SQL; logical reads via Extended Events. After onboarding, compare scan count on Orders table for new tenant_id. EF Core 8+ tagged queries appear in logs. Interview story: API p95 2s → missing (TenantId, CreatedAt) index + N+1 on Lines → fixed with projection and index → p95 80ms — cache optional afterward.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Jumping to Redis without showing SQL. Not knowing N+1. Saying AsNoTracking helps writes. Unable to read basic execution plan seek vs scan.

interviewTakeaways: EF Core performance = correct SQL shape, indexes, AsNoTracking reads, avoid N+1, then optional cache.
When not to use EF: heavy reporting aggregations — consider raw SQL or read replica.
Production tip: composite indexes on tenant + sort columns; UPDATE STATISTICS after bulk onboarding imports.

60s: Log SQL, read plan for scan vs seek. Project DTOs AsNoTracking. Fix N+1 with Include split or Select. Index WHERE and ORDER BY columns. Compiled query for hot path. Cache only after query is fast.
Follow-up: offset pagination vs cursor pagination at ten million rows?
commonPitfalls: Saying 'add Redis' first gets you rejected — masking scan on ten million rows still hits DB on miss.
Include five levels deep on list endpoint — cartesian explosion and megabytes per request.
Strong answer: 'After onboarding, Orders scan on TenantId — added IX_TenantId_CreatedAt, projected DTO, split query on Lines, p95 2s to 90ms per dotnet trace SQL dependency.'
